section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a cross-sectional study involving 607 healthy adults, investigating the relationship between dispositional gratitude and self-reported physical health symptoms. The study explored whether this relationship is mediated by reduced levels of perceived loneliness and stress. Serial mediation analysis revealed that the positive effect of gratitude on physical health was significantly mediated by lower reported levels of perceived loneliness and stress, suggesting gratitude may buffer against stress and loneliness and improve somatic health.
